text:
anya: quick sync — I ran a focused bring-up for the new 13B-chat variant with int4 quant on our main assistant slice. some headline numbers below, and a proposal for a hybrid routing experiment.

mike: pls drop the exact slice and run config when you have a sec.

anya: slice = prod-assistant: short/long mix (50/50); samples=10k users, 3-turn avg. run script: `./run_eval.sh --model x13b-chat --quant int4 --seq 2048 --batch 8`

priya: quick numbers?

anya: int8 baseline (current prod): p95 latency = 340ms, cost/token ~$0.012, composite-quality = 0.812
anya: int4 result (single-model): p95 latency = 150ms, cost/token ~$0.003, composite-quality = 0.794 (-0.018 absolute)

mike: so ~2.3x latency improvement and ~4x cost reduction, quality drop ~2.2% relative. good. did you look at hallucination or safety regressions?

anya: quick QA on safety slices: small uptick in hallucination on factual QA (0.6% -> 1.4%). we flagged examples. not catastrophic but noticeable for query types with long context.

priya: hmm. product will push back on any QA/regression. what hybrid idea do you have?

anya: proposal: routing policy by prompt length + task type. rules:
- short user prompts (<120 tokens) + high-sensitivity intents -> route to int8
- long context / low-sensitivity (assistant chatter, summarization) -> int4
- fallback chain: if int4 output fails safety check -> replay on int8 and mark for offline eval

mike: prefer flagging + gradual rollout. do we have feature to route by intent classifier?

infra-bot: note: can enable route-by-tag in canary for 1% traffic per region. add config `routing.policy.hybrid_quant = "enabled"`

david: what's the expected unit economics at 50/50 split by traffic?

anya: back-of-envelope: if 50% int8, 50% int4 -> effective cost/token = 0.5*0.012 + 0.5*0.003 = $0.0075 (~38% reduction vs full int8). latency p95 will be a mix; critical paths still see int8 ~340ms, but bulk long tails improved.

priya: product ask: can we meet a 1% max quality regression SLA for GTN? current drop is 2.2% if all int4. hybrid looks like maybe ~0.8%? need sim.

anya: I ran a weighted sim on our slice with routing heuristic above: predicted composite-quality delta = -0.9% abs (meets 1% threshold) and cost reduction ~36%.

mike: nice. what's operational risk? cache/keying differences?

anya: KV cache format identical. main ops differences: two model variants to keep warm (int8/int4) and routing logic. small increase in memory footprint for model sets but within Dedicated pool limits. autoscale policy needs to account for different throughput per-model.

priya: okay — next steps for GTN proposal: 1) assemble 50 sample failure cases for product review, 2) enable 1% canary with routing policy and safety replay, 3) run 7-day smoke with monitoring alerts for hallucination rate and latency.

mike: I'll own canary infra and alert thresholds. any suggestions for thresholds?

david: set alert if hallucination rate increases by >0.5pp absolute or composite-quality drops >0.7% over baseline in 1h window.

anya: noted. I'll push PR with the sample examples and the routing config. linking to quick diff in draft: https://go/rdw/quant-hybrid-draft (internal).

priya: thanks — if the canary looks good we can present to GTN next Wed. :thumbsup:

mike: +1

infra-bot: deploy job queued: `deploy-hybrid-quant-canary` — ETA 12:00 UTC tomorrow.

anya: thanks everyone, will follow up with PR and the sample pack.
